title: Iran says Pakistan's army chief to visit Tehran on Monday
gist: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir is set to visit Tehran on Monday as Pakistan continues acting as mediator in the stalled US-Iran war negotiations.

insights.claim: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir will visit Tehran on Monday, per Iran's foreign ministry, as part of Pakistan's continued mediation between Iran and the United States.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Watch for any signal from this visit on whether Iran-US negotiations to end their war are edging back toward a formal track, which would matter for Strait of Hormuz risk premia and Iran-linked sanctions trades.
insights.quote: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir will visit Tehran on Monday, Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Sunday, according to a statement by the ministry.

insights.claim: Pakistan has formally taken on the mediator role in negotiations between Iran and the United States aimed at ending their war.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A functioning third-party channel (Pakistan) is a structural precondition for any eventual Iran-US de-escalation deal; its continued activity is a leading indicator worth tracking alongside direct signals from Washington and Tehran.
insights.quote: Pakistan has taken on the mediator role in negotiations between Iran and the U.S. aimed at ending their war.

insights.claim: A quadrilateral meeting involving the United States, Iran, Pakistan and Qatar was held at the Burgenstock hotel complex in Switzerland on June 21, 2026, indicating an established multilateral diplomatic channel around the Iran conflict predates this Tehran visit.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Confirms Qatar and Pakistan both sit inside the diplomatic architecture around the Iran-US conflict, useful for mapping which regional actors have leverage or exposure if a settlement framework advances.
